I add a screen language without replacing the firmware. This page prepares a single script with a ready-made translation (Polish, Czech or your own, e.g. any European language) and you run it with one command from your computer. Unofficial, use at your own risk.

After a restart the screen speaks Polish or Czech. About 10 minutes in total.

What you need (10 minutes, you cannot break anything)

  • A computer with Windows 10/11 or a Mac, connected to the same Wi‑Fi network as the printer.
  • The Snapmaker U1 switched on and idle (nothing printing).
  • You can return to the original with one script from this page (it also removes the yellow bar).
  • Mini glossary: the Terminal is a window where you paste a command. SSH is a secure remote connection from the computer to the printer. You do not need to understand more.

Step 1: enable Root Access

This is the only thing you do on the printer screen. Without it the printer will not accept a connection from your computer. The screen is in English because that is the factory language.

Video from the emulator; the screen looks the same as on the printer: cube icon → Maintenance → Root Access → scroll the declaration → Agree → Open.

What this means (manufacturer's declaration): after enabling root the printer may stop supporting official OTA updates and some cloud features. Enabling it does not void the warranty by itself, but damage caused by changes to the system may. After the installation you can turn it off in the same place with Close Root Access.
The same steps as screenshots

  1. Cube icon on the left, then scroll to Maintenance

  2. Maintenance → Root Access

  3. Scroll the declaration to the end and tick Agree

  4. Open: “Root Access Granted”

Made for the original Snapmaker firmware. On paxx12 I tested the scripts only in an emulator, not on a printer. On paxx12 and other modifications you use them at your own risk.

Step 2: prepare and run the script

Three things: the printer address, the language and (optionally) the settings. You get a ready command right below.

A. Printer address

Easiest on the printer itself: tap the cube icon (Settings) and open Wi‑Fi. Once it is connected to the network, the printer shows the network name and its IP address there. The address is four numbers separated by dots, e.g. 192.168.0.100. Type it below (only numbers and dots).

I cannot see the address on the printer: other ways
  1. In your router: open your router's page (usually 192.168.0.1 or 192.168.1.1; the password is often on a sticker) and look at the list of connected devices. The U1 usually appears there as lava (sometimes Snapmaker), with its address next to it.
  2. On your phone: a home-network scanner app (e.g. Fing) lists devices with their addresses. Look for the name lava or the maker Snapmaker.
  3. In your slicer (Snapmaker Orca, OrcaSlicer): when you add a network printer its address is usually shown.

Enter the plain number address here. A name such as U1.local does not work on this printer.

Advanced settings (SSH port)
SSH port: 22 by default. Another port only makes sense with the emulator (e.g. 2222) or port forwarding.

B. Language

After installing

Choose one language. Only one works on the screen at a time. To change it, choose another one on this page and run the script again (you cannot pick new languages in the printer menu).

Bar at the bottom of the screen

Without this, technical messages and a yellow IP address would appear at the bottom of the screen. Leave it ticked unless you want to see them.

Technical details (you do not need to read this)

For the language to survive a restart, the printer needs the file /oem/.debug. With it, the screen shows Klipper messages and a yellow IP address at the bottom. This option hides the file while the screen starts and gives it back right away (verified on a real U1). Untick it if you prefer to add nothing besides the language files.

What exactly does this option hide? (photos from a real U1)

This is how the printer screen looks without hiding, when the file /oem/.debug exists. The first photo is the Polish home screen, the other two were taken while starting a print (screen in Czech). With hiding enabled these two elements are gone.

The bar shows for a few seconds for every message from the printer and covers the lower edge of the screen (including buttons). It does not affect printing, but it looks like an error and gets in the way.

Language menu on the printer: do not choose anything in it after the installation, because it may restore a built-in language. The language is not in the menu (the list is built into the screen program), so you change it with this page and the script: pick another language and run the script again.

C. Download the script and run it

Testers welcome, especially on Windows! Send the result (works, does not work, what the window showed): Issues.

1) Check the connection (changes nothing; after entering the password it should print OK):

2) Download the script:

⚠️ Warning: after returning to the original, Wi‑Fi on the printer may turn off. Run it only when you can reach the screen: after the restart open Settings → Wi‑Fi, turn the network on and check the IP address.

Return to original: removes added languages, sets English (if an added language was active), removes the yellow bar and restarts the printer. It clears the whole overlay, so other add-ons stored there disappear too. You can then close Root Access on the screen.

A shortcut: double-click instead of pasting commands. It is the same script packed into one file.

What happens after you run it:

  1. A text window opens (Terminal on Mac, a black window on Windows).
  2. You type the printer IP address.
  3. You type the root password (characters are not shown).
  4. The script checks that the printer is not printing. If it is, nothing changes.
  5. Installing a language: adds and selects the language, hides the yellow bar (if the option is ticked) and restarts the screen. It goes black for about a minute.
  6. Return to original: removes added languages and the yellow bar, clears the overlay (including other add-ons) and restarts the printer.
  7. After Done. press Enter to close the window.

⚠️ Warning: after returning to the original, Wi‑Fi on the printer may turn off. Run it only when you can reach the screen: after the restart open Settings → Wi‑Fi, turn the network on and check the IP address.

Mac: download the ZIP with the double-click files and unpack it. A single file downloaded with the buttons below will not run on double-click without execute permission.
If macOS blocks the file after downloading: first check which folder your browser saves downloads to (Safari: Settings → General; Chrome: Settings → Downloads). In the commands below replace example_folder_name with the name of that folder, e.g. Downloads, or Downloads/U1-launcher-mac after unpacking the ZIP. Then run these commands in Terminal, in order:

xattr -d com.apple.quarantine "$HOME/example_folder_name/U1-install-polish.command"
chmod +x "$HOME/example_folder_name/U1-install-polish.command"
bash "$HOME/example_folder_name/U1-install-polish.command"
For Czech, change the filename to U1-install-czech.command; for returning to original, use U1-return-to-original.command.
“Apple could not verify” message: this is normal for unsigned files. Do not move it to the Trash: click Done, open System Settings → Privacy & Security, click Open Anyway at the bottom and run the file again.

Double-click file names: U1-install-polish, U1-install-czech, U1-return-to-original (.command on Mac, .bat on Windows).

Double-click file: what it is and what it needs

Instead of pasting a command into Terminal or the command prompt, you download one file and open it with a double-click. It asks for the printer IP address, connects over SSH (it asks for the password) and runs the same script you see here; you can read it at the end of the file in a text editor. It takes the chosen language and the bar option from the settings above, and you do not need to type the IP address here.

  • Mac: macOS with Terminal (the ssh command is built in); scripts checked on macOS 27.3. Permissions and the first run are described in the box above.
  • Windows: Windows 10 version 1809 or newer, or Windows 11, with the OpenSSH Client (check: ssh -V; enable it in Settings, Apps, Optional features) and PowerShell 5.1. Windows may show a SmartScreen warning (More info, Run anyway) because the file is not signed. The Windows version has not been tested on a real Windows; if it fails, use the commands in the step below.
  • Printer: firmware 2.1.2.159 (the only version checked), Root Access enabled, same Wi‑Fi network.

A side note: other languages and alphabets

Not part of the installer. The page installs Polish, Czech or your own language file. Below are the results of my tests on single screens with sample strings; no native readers reviewed them.

What I checked

  • Latin (except Romanian Ț ț), Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese display without extra changes.
  • Romanian and Korean were shown in the emulator and on the printer (they need changes beyond this page).
  • Arabic, Hindi and Thai were shown correctly in the emulator after extra work. Not checked on the printer in this form.
  • Snapmaker has announced official Korean, Arabic, Portuguese, Japanese and Italian, among others.

Korean

Many alphabets at once (each row in a different language)

Custom language (e.g. Slovak, Hungarian)

Translate two files and install them with this same page. The language will not appear in the printer menu (the list is built in), but the screen will use it after you run the script.

Which alphabets the screen supports: see “Which languages will work”.

  1. Download the English reference files (screen texts from firmware 2.1.2.159):
  2. Translate the values only. Leave the keys (e.g. "cancel"), the placeholders %s, %d, {…} and the _meta entry unchanged. In language_name put the name of the language. Save as UTF‑8.
  3. Choose a language code and your files:
    two letters, a hyphen, two capital letters; it cannot be one of the 9 built-in codes

The files are not sent anywhere: they are read in your browser and end up only in the downloaded script. The page checks keys and placeholders against the English reference, and the script on the printer checks them again.

Help

When something does not work: common errors

When something does not work

  • Connection refused: Root Access is not enabled (step 1) or the IP address is wrong.
  • “REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED” (changed host key warning): the printer has a new SSH key, which happens after the overlay is cleared, after a firmware update or after a reinstall. If this is your printer on your own network, remove the old entry with ssh-keygen -R PRINTER_ADDRESS and run the command again. Nothing was changed on the printer, because the login stopped before the script.
  • Permission denied: the password. On the original firmware 2.1.2.159 in the emulator snapmaker worked; if it does not work on your printer, do not keep guessing, check whether you changed it earlier.
  • “ssh” is not recognized (Windows): Settings → Apps → Optional features → add “OpenSSH Client”.
  • The script cannot read the state or the printer is not ready: check the connection and the printer state, then try again when it is neither printing nor paused.
  • Screen in English after a firmware update: the update may have removed the language files. Check compatibility and run the script again.
  • You want to return to the original: download the “return to original” script in step 2 and run it like the install script. It removes added languages and the yellow bar, clears the overlay (including other add-ons) and restarts the printer. On the next SSH connection your computer may report REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED.

Warranty and liability

Warranty, liability and other important matters

  • This is an unofficial and independent project. It is not affiliated with or supported by Snapmaker. “Snapmaker” is a trademark of its owner.
  • No warranty from the author. The script and the translations are provided “as is”, without any warranty, including fitness for a particular purpose. You use them at your own risk; to the extent permitted by law the author gives no warranty and accepts no liability for the effects of use. This disclaimer does not limit rights that cannot be excluded.
  • Printer warranty. The manufacturer states in the “Root Access” declaration on the screen that enabling root access alone does not automatically void the warranty, but damage caused by changes to the system may. Read that declaration on the printer before ticking “Agree”.
  • Updates. After enabling root the printer may stop supporting official OTA updates, remote diagnostics and some cloud features. A firmware update may remove the added language files; after an update check that it still works and install again if needed.
  • Security. Root Access weakens the printer's protection on the network. Enable it only on a trusted home network. The default password is publicly known, so after the installation turn the access off (Settings → Maintenance → Root Access → Close Root Access) or change the password.
  • What the script does and does not do. It does not change the original system files or the firmware; it adds files in the overlay and changes one setting. It also leaves the /oem/.debug flag, through which the overlay remembers other system writes. The “return to original” script removes added languages and the flag, then restarts the printer, which clears the whole overlay (including other add-ons). It does not disable Root Access and does not revert changes stored outside the overlay.
  • The translations were made from the English version of the firmware. They may contain mistakes or be too long for the screen. The Czech has not been checked by a Czech speaker.
  • Do not connect to printers that are not yours, and do not run the script during a print.
